lines.text: A lot of things were wrong with that shot: the Falostesse was the wrong choice, his shoulders were raised, but above all -- he cannot trust his eyesight.
You know, you don't feel like too bad of a shot yourself...
You hear an explosion within the weapon in your hands. The branches of the pinetree behind the girl shake ever so lightly. Your ears are still ringing...
A plume of smoke erupts from the barrel. Your hand goes numb from the explosion. With your ears still ringing you lower the weapon to see what happened.
Ask for another shot. You'll get it with the next one, the god damn light reflected off some window, surely...
The sound of the explosion from your gun echoes over all of Martinaise. The bullet found its way to the heart of a kid.
It came out wrong, you made it sound like you're some sort of roulette addict looking for a fix, ask again, more controlled this time:
Feels like shit man, how did this happen? Hit him straight in the chest... how horrible, you're so sorry.
The buckle explodes into tiny pieces, coming loose with a *whirr*.
Your hand twitches. A single bullet hidden from sight. Remember the way it slides into the barrel. The muzzle of the loaded weapon pointed at your heart -- it feels familiar, doesn't it?
Then we'll be *ready* for them.
We were sort of hoping there would be a gun, an expensive jewel, or at least a *sword* in it for you -- if you deliver the message. Oh well...
Your fingers trace the edges of an imaginary holster on your hip. A slight twitch runs through your index finger.
God... even this javelin-throwing freak here...
An extremely inadvisable strategy against automatic weapons. Be sure not to make the same mistake.
Fire off a shot over her head and use the moment of confusion to close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
No... no-no-no-no. THEY'RE REALLY NOT. The gun wasn't even loaded. No shots fired. You're fine.
She's frantic, confused, teetering under all that gear... There's an opening, if you just move fast enough.
Alright, this is how we do it: You hurl the tare bag in her face -- already darting right -- and *immediately* close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Alright, here's how we do it: As soon as that gun isn't pointed at you again, you dash right, then immediately close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
She's frantic, confused, teetering under all that gear... There's an opening, if you just move fast enough... If not, the lieutenant's got her on his sights.
Oh... I see. Okay, the gun was empty. All is good. You're fine.
Here's the plan: You jerk left, dash right, close the distance and cut her hand off. Ready?

Here's the plan: Shine the light straight in her eye and immediately dart right-- the light will blind her, allowing you to close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Okay, you need to figure out what to do with her now.
Alright, this is how we do it: You fling the prybar at her-- already darting right -- and *immediately* close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Here's the plan: Drop the multitool and immediately dart right -- the noise will startle her, allowing you to close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Alright, here's the plan: You fling the chaincutters in her face -- already darting right -- and *immediately* close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Porta-reel is the key. Up the volume to the *MAX* and hit 'Play'. The sound will startle her, allowing you to close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
The gun, throw it in her face -- she won't see it coming. As she tries to catch or evade, you close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Alright, here's the plan: You hurl the ledger in her face -- already darting right -- and *immediately* close the distance. Left hand grabs the barrel, right one breaks the wrist...
Sure, you're you. But how do we end this? She's not just gonna let you leave.
Maybe this would be a good wall for dodge ball?
He wants so badly to draw his Armistice, but he also doesn't *want* to want to draw it.
You place every box with the utmost delicacy and precision.
He's practically itching to stick that thing in someone's face and pull the trigger.
No wonder the communards couldn't shoot straight -- they were too shagged out!
There's a word on the tip of your tongue, a name: 'Egret.' Don't ask us what it means, we're not sure.
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
Feisty little thing! But don't worry -- it's under control.
This splash was obviously made with a clumsy hand. Perhaps it adds to the artistry?
The coin narrowly slips by your out-stretched fingers and falls to the ground.
The coin lands into your hand as if it has always belonged there. The swallow returns.
His moves are quick and precise as he first checks the weapon, then aims it at the sea. This man knows firearms *intimately*.
Nearly the same sound produced by the action on a good breechloader, you can't fail to notice.
There's no way you'd catch that cigarette anyway.
Yes, really. Don't even try. You'll just embarrass yourself.
Mr. Smooth Moves! You snatch the dice out of the air with one hand, just like you're in a movie.
She winked back at you! Can you believe it? You truly are Mr. Smooth Moves!
She smiled at you. She smiled! You truly are Mr. Smooth Moves!

You overthink it. Your hands can't agree what to do and the two dice drop to the floor and scatter in opposite directions, like pearls from a broken string. The blue one disappears down the pit in the centre of the room...
If you want to try again, then you need to have the prybar in your *hand*, detective.
You need to have the Kvalsund KR+2 Multi-Tool in your *hand*, detective.
An old Belle-Magrave rifle, Revolutionary-era. Prized for its reliability more than it's accuracy. The rest are probably Belle-Magraves too, just too damaged to be identified.
An old Belle-Magrave rifle, Revolutionary-era. Prized for its reliability more than it's accuracy. The rest are probably Belle-Magraves too, just too damaged to be sure.
Factory balanced... bakelite and stainless steel.
But not when you're in a *tight* spot.
You throw the bomb and it's way off.
Shoot him in the mouth. Shoot him before he shoots you.
This time feels different. You aim higher -- as if pulled by a magnet. Your hand goes numb from the explosion and a plume of smoke erupts from the gun...
The smoke drifts west with the wind. You hear the plaza erupt in violence, slow, like a waterfall in reverse.
A plume of smoke and fire erupts from the gun and your hand goes numb from the explosion...
This third one -- he is the most dangerous of them all. Heavily armed.
This third one -- he is the most dangerous of them all. Heavily armed.
A small explosion expels the bullet from the chamber. With a puff of smoke it hits the man square in the chest -- producing a soft clicking sound in the armour.
No. It's off. *Way* off. I told you.
With a crash of shattering glass and a terrible roar the fire draws in oxygen -- the bomb hits the mercenary in the chest,  swallowing him in flames as he staggers backward.
An unbelievable shot from the lieutenant.
Another soft explosion, like a firecracker goes off in your hand. Another soft *click* from the gleaming white cuirass.
You really, really should have a gun in your hand by now -- or *something* dangerous. This feels *scary*.
0.4 seconds remain. There are six little black dots in the tip of the barrel, like a honeycomb. This is a *nock cannon*. It shoots six rounds in one pull of the trigger.
0.6 seconds remain. There are six little black dots in the tip of the thick barrel, like a honeycomb. This is a *nock cannon*. It shoots six rounds in one pull of the trigger.
The sharp blade chafes against your skin, producing a scratching sound. The surface underneath the beard feels tender, the air brushing against it chilly.
Stop, for crying out loud! You're gonna cut your own throat.
Your hand trembles as you scratch at your cheek... oh no, that's not how a grown man shaves!
They feel so smooth, surprisingly so. A feeling of freshness overcomes you, as if you just came from a cold bath.
Beneath the doubt sprouts a new vigour, like you've discarded some bad decisions. It feels as though you've passed through a ritual. Emerged from cold water, even...
The razor lands with a *clang*. A red trickle begins to spread in the water.
Thank god, I would have cut your throat.
Your hand shakes so hard you can't even muster up the courage to *try*. Maybe you're just too *wild* at heart?
Like an artist with a brush or a master swordsman, you use the small mirror and the straight razor -- with some soap -- to remove all that unkempt hair from below the nose-line.
Your hand refuses to move another millimetre. A small trickle of blood runs down your cheek.
The sharp blade chafes against your skin, producing a scratching sound. The surface underneath the beard feels tender, the air brushing against it chilly.
This is dangerous. You're 70% certain you always leave your gun loaded.
It's extra ammunition. She's locked and loaded, ready to fight some cops.
The kid moves his hands like a basketball player dribbling fast.
Oh fuck, it was loaded... There were two bullets in it. You always keep at least two barrels loaded.
It was loaded. There were two bullets in it. You always keep at least two barrels  loaded.
It's me. I'm keeping his hand from moving. We're not doing that anymore. We're not reading those words. People have died. He needs to work, not ache his heart for something that will never return.
This little thing could reveal much about the weapon that shot it.
If you were to prick him with something sharp you could see it oozing out -- a knife, maybe? No -- a rapier!
The muzzle-loaders need to be reloaded after every one or two shots -- the automatics every one or two *minutes*.
The muzzle-loaders need to be reloaded after every one, two -- or in your case three -- shots, the automatics every one or two *minutes*.
Rooty-tooty pointy shooty!
A door-gun is a gun mounted to the door of a transport airship. They have a habit of mowing down civilians. Farmers mostly.
Why not? Military fortifications are made for that kind of thing.
You catch a single white flower between your fingers. The rest fly off into the wind. It's a may bell!
Your 9mm semiautomatic finger pistols produce a satisfying snap. (Strange for such a low calibre finger-gun to sound so chunky.) The flower in your hand is impressed. So is Kim.
Probably for the best -- your 9mm semiautomatic finger pistols are not a toy to be waved around.
Your 9mm semiautomatic finger pistols make two satisfying snaps. (Strange for such a small calibre of finger pistol to sound so chunky.) The flower in your hand is impressed. So is she.
...the wind brushes them off the roof. They're gone.
Just as you look at the flowers, a gust of wind raises them from the roof, picking them up in the air...
This is clearly a sport for him. Something like archery -- or darts?
A miss.
This is clearly sports for him. Something like archery -- or darts?
Another hit. The lieutenant looks at you -- in acknowledgement.
A direct hit. The lieutenant looks at you -- in acknowledgement."
In honour of that *precise* forensic remark, officer. A real hit.
In honour of another *precise* forensic observation.
He sounds a *tiny bit* sorry he did not find it before you got hit.
It probably is... fucking butterfingers.
Kid would make a half-decent sharpshooter, no?
He says he's not, but his hand moves instinctively toward his holster as he studies the note.
Harry, this reminds you -- you're out of bullets.
Cheek against the cheek rest, hand on the hair trigger. On a calm day like this...
Cheek against the cheek rest, hand on the hair trigger. On a calm day like this...
Still warm from his parched hands. Not the metal. The metal is ice cold. This weapon has been modified several times.
It has stayed true to him. He can still make it sing.
It has stayed true to him. He can still make it sing.
That was not the death blow yet. You saved yourself -- for now. Keep stumbling around and it *will* happen.
The DEATH BLOW is coming.
We can do it, brother. You have it in the nerve endings in your hand. You just need to dig into your muscle memory.
Unstable is good, actually. She will be easier to disarm... no wait, actually unstable is pretty bad.
With a police baton. Like a crook or someone.
That's an Ister 50. A Zsiemsk-made monstrosity. It'll blow your head clean off.
Firearm! A Glace 08, or a .38 calibre pistol -- either is small enough for you to have missed.
Ah yes, of course. Good catch -- go ahead:
Unless it was an exceptional, almost godly sniper.
You are prepared. Don't put away your friend. Your weapon.
You are prepared. Don't put away your friend. Your weapon.
For God's sake -- find some bullets before you go any further. An unloaded gun won't do you any good!
For God's sake -- find some bullets before you go any further. An unloaded gun won't do you any good!
What you have isn't enough. You'll need more firepower. A ranged weapon.
For God's sake -- find some bullets before you go any further. An unloaded gun won't do you any good!
Not true. He purposefully over-aimed and shot the window -- you had him second guessing himself. Only for a second. Do not assume he will miss the next time.
A Kiejl Model 40 revolver. Eight rounds in the barrel. The gun slowly sways in his hand -- from the inebriation.
A Kiejl Model 40 revolver. Eight rounds in the barrel. The gun slowly sways in his hand -- from the inebriation.
Technically, the other man has the biggest gun, but... we're beyond that now.
The angle of the paint drops reveals that they were fired at the canvas with the force of a hand cannon.
A rifle. Revolutionary-period. Your bullet looks to be an old 4.46 mm -- from the surplus left over from the turn of the century. Probably an antique or a retrofitted antique.
Antiques enthusiasts, guerrilla fighters in distant countries, a few lucky Jamrock bangers. You're looking for the same thing you found in that hidden weapons cache -- only in working order.

The 4.46 calibre was widely used with the *Belle-Magrave* rifle, a Revacholian manufacturer. The B-M dominated the battlefields of the Insulindian theatre of the Antecentennial Revolution, 50 years ago.

Incidentally, you have just such a rifle with you. The dusty old thing you found hidden in the basement below the commercial area. It's unusable, sadly. If it were, the bullet would *probably* fit the chamber.
You can't remember what happened last week -- what makes you think you're going to remember arcane firearm models?
Antiques enthusiasts, guerrilla fighters in distant countries, a few lucky Jamrock bangers. You're looking for a well-preserved antique, most likely.

No, but Zieleger, a major firearm manufacturer, ended up with a surplus after the war, so there are still a lot of these old military rifles floating around, usually broken. The quality was appalling.
Three mercenaries, no doubt armed to the teeth, hungry for vengeance... You've only got muzzle loaders. This isn't looking good.
If she kills herself you'll get her gun...
This does look like an *embrasure*, a slit made for shooting out of.
This is such a wipeout.
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
Your hand moves, smooth and lightning-fast, to the holster -- you whip out the gun.
Sorry, boiadeiro, the moment has passed. You just won't look cool anymore.
You grab hold of the grip and pull hard, but it won't budge. The gun is caught on the seam inside your jacket.
You're only making things worse. The jacket is going to rip if you continue.
Nope. It's stuck in there good.
My favourite was the gun he lost.
My favourite is the gun.
My favourite is the gun.
My favourite is the gun he lost.
He could definitely work more on his Hand/Eye Coordination...
He can't even walk straight. How did he write your name in cathode rays?
The writer has *never* held a sword in their life, let alone two two-handed swords at the same time.
"Always aim for the centre of mass"?
Something about it was completely unnatural. Corrupted. Your muscle memory knew what to do and went for it, but there were gaps...
You are immediately surprised by the ball's lack of weight. No matter. You'll make it work.
It felt like you were going for a thrust or a lunge -- there was definitely gonna be jumping. Maybe you scored a point, but this is a *fiasco*.
The cold metal ball is surprisingly smooth against your neck. It has a pattern on it. (Probably a sponsored ball.) Yours would only be covered with bumps of learning and scars of victory.
A chilly breeze ruffles your hair as you stand there, feet firmly planted. All sounds, smells, even the wind -- everything fades until the only thing left is the union of Man and Ball.
An embodiment of pure motion. A fine-tuned *locomotor* running at maximum efficiency.
Already your muscles are adjusting to the weight, the nervous system calibrating, until you and the ball have merged into a single entity. The *manball* is ready.
This felt... wrong. Wrong like touching your sister's breast. You threw your sister's breast.
Nip it in the bud, before it gets completely out of hand. Right on his cheek. Just a light tap... to scare him a little. Don't kill him.
Nip it in the bud, before it gets completely out of hand. Right on his cheek. Just a light tap... to scare him a little. It won't kill him.
Not today, badge.
You got it all right! You're showing it to him, victorious. They're *seeing* the badge.
At last! The fastest hand in Revachol reunited with the slickest tool in North. You're gonna be the envy of the town, baby!
This is your gun. Now if we could only find your personality...

This is your gun and in the world of unarmed civilians a man with a gun is king. But in a wholesome and life-affirming way. You just keep the wheels of the world spinning and maybe there's some money to be made on the side?
Holding the gun feels natural and satisfying. It's like an extension of your arm, the polished wooden handle almost fusing into your palm.
This is your gun. Yours and -- by extension -- the People's. But mostly yours. Now go and serve the People.
Sheathe your sidearm, officer. A serious law official -- cop-by-the-book -- should know to only unholster their service weapon when using it is unavoidable.
A Villiers 9mm pistol -- where Insulindian steel meets Revachol craftsmanship. With it thou wilt protect the fair people of thine homeland and keep the *visitors* in check.

This is your gun. It's more of a symbol than anything else, because there is always, *ALWAYS* a rational, sensible, reasonable solution to every situation. Sheathe it and know: You have the moral high-ground.
It reminds you of the day you first held it. With fear and respect. Hoping you don't have to use it -- in vain. The sun was out in Jamrock. It was so long ago...
The pig iron's yours, boss. You should blaze one right now to celebrate... and then shoot some cans or chickens or something.
This gun -- Sunrise, Parabellum -- will be the only thing standing between you and the all-consuming nothingness that threatens to eat the world. Sheathe it and wait, Herald. It won't be long now.
The gun -- your gun -- can be an item of destruction, but *also* creation. The Villiers-LaSalle Art Project. Time to shoot some beauty through the heart of Martinaise.
This is your gun. It's angry at you for losing it. Everyone is. The least you can do is press your lips against the cold steel to apologize... and then just try to go on living.
Although only useful against assailants made of flesh and blood, the gun is still yours. Maybe Remote Viewers also have some other... non-conventional weaponry?
Be careful now, slow and steady does it. Make him repeat it first.
Click.
Click.
The gun. The murder weapon is the perfect opener.
No-no. Be careful now, slow and steady does it. Make him repeat it first.
Click.
Oh no, you were wrong. Don't listen to your *hands* for god's sake, you're too close...
The calibre of bullet he used does not do that kind of damage.
If only he had the ammunition.
He means murder weapon.
Slam the weapon man, the murder weapon.
It certainly does not help with aiming...
You know how you'd be best off here? With a gun. I'd be the star of the show if you only had a working gun.
You know how you'd be best off here? With a gun. Best have it in your hand when you go in there.
Your fingers wrap around the handle, the index slides into the trigger loop. Do it. Go on!
So that's *one* dead and a looooong reload. But whatever.
Doesn't that tingle in your index finger give it away?
You know the answer already. The tingle in your index finger gave it away.
And something you'll do again, before this is all over.
As you look at them you feel your index finger reflexively contract three times.
A memory, an echo in the recesses of your amygdala.
You're so close! Almost there. Ultimate dexterity is within reach...
You're so close! Almost there. Ultimate dexterity is within reach...
A pilgrimage you can make with just your hand.
Sure is!
C'mon! Beauty is inviting you on a pilgrimage. A pilgrimage you can make with just your hand.
His hands lead the way when it comes to that. And his shoulders. It's reflex.
Target practice. For improving your aim. Some of us have been wondering when you'll get around to that.
Oh no...
Better, but practice makes perfect! One more time -- right into the seabull's eye!
There! On the ice. Target practice.
It's a seagull. They're practically immortal. And the only thing you'll be throwing is some dirt. It's guaranteed no one will get hurt.
Told you we needed to practice! What if this was a combat situation? We wouldn't be talking anymore. Try again!
Precisely. No obstructions, just the seagull. Pick up some dirt and throw it at the bird. Come on, hurry up!
